nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Sustainable water resource management|Green infrastructure planning_qna_000
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What issue does the paragraph mention regarding the stakeholders involved in green infrastructure projects in Ghana?
nodes.answer: The findings generalized to cover a broad group of stakeholders do not reflect the perspective of the built environment on the knowledge of the multifunctional attributes of GI.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Sustainable water resource management|Green infrastructure planning_qna_001
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What is the main focus of the study discussed in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The study focuses on the adoption and implementation success of Green Infrastructure (GI) by effectively conveying its multifunctional prospects and considering client objectives.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Sustainable water resource management|Green infrastructure planning_qna_002
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What issue has been observed in Ghana's green infrastructure (GI) development, particularly in Kumasi?
nodes.answer: GI in Ghana has increasingly become fragmented despite the volume of green space development, attributed to a lack of effective planning for GI systems.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Sustainable water resource management|Green infrastructure planning_qna_003
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What gaps does the study aim to address regarding green infrastructure (GI) in developing regions?
nodes.answer: The study aims to fill the knowledge gap regarding the multifunctional attributes of GI systems among built environment professionals in developing regions.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Sustainable water resource management|Green infrastructure planning_qna_004
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What is inadequately represented in the European strategy on Green Infrastructure (GI) regarding biodiversity?
nodes.answer: The ecological landscape perspective necessary for the conservation of biodiversity is inadequately represented in the European strategy on GI.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean water and sanitation|Sustainable water resource management|Green infrastructure planning_qna_005
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What factors must be considered when implementing green infrastructure to address biodiversity loss effectively?
nodes.answer: Trade-offs between other intended outcomes must be explicitly considered when implementing green infrastructure.
